Airtable website, 2018

Airtable’s 2018 home page: five blue- and pink-skinned figures with long bending limbs climb, lift, and pass shapes to each other beside the heading “Create, your way”.

The live Airtable site has changed since this 2018 capture.

Observed

  • The heading “Create, your way” is set in a dark grey sans-serif of regular weight, with grey body text, a grey email field, and a blue “Get started” button with small rounded corners.
  • On the right, five figures form a human tower: one sits on a yellow circle and draws a line with a pen, one kneels on another’s back with a laptop, one lunges to lift a figure above.
  • Skin is blue on all figures; hair is black; clothes are coral pink, yellow, and blue, some with small white doodles or dots.
  • Pink and pale blue blocks, yellow circles, a blue triangle, and teal potted plants are stacked around them.
  • The fills are flat with a light speckled grain; there are no outlines. A pale lilac curve starts the next section, where a purple app window appears.

Why it belongs

It shows the style’s core metaphor of teamwork: many bendy figures assembling simple shapes into a structure, which also stands for the product’s building blocks.

Borrow

Show collaboration as figures physically stacking or passing simple geometric blocks.
